sentences.text:
Author: T. Vinod Kumar Bench: T. Vinod Kumar  THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE T. VINOD KUMAR  WRIT PETITION No.25596 of 2008 ORDER:
None appears for the petitioner.

Heard Sri Praveen Kumar Veerjala, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 and 2, Sri M.Ramu, learned Standing counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.3 and 4, learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.5 and 6, and Sri P.Shashi Kiran, learned counsel for the 7th respondent,
and perused the record.
2. Shorn of unnecessary details, the case of the petitioner in brief is that he is the owner and possessor of land in Sy.No.116/aa3 admeasuring Ac.0.22 guntas situated in Mailardevpally village,
Rajendranagar Mandalo, Ranga Reddy District abutting to old Kurnool road; and that he had sold some land to third parties thereby leaving with him the land to an extent of 600 sq. yards in the aforesaid survey number.
3. It is the contention of the petitioner that the respondent authorities have converted the old Kunool road into 150 feet road and for the aforesaid purpose, have taken his land admeasuring 600 sq. yards without giving any notice or without following due procedure as contemplated under the Land Acquisition Act.
4.

Petitioner further contends that the on the respondent authorities taking his land without paying any compensation, he got a notice issued through his counsel on 22-10-2008 requesting the respondents to pay compensation in respect of his land which has been taken for laying the road.

5. Petitioner further contends that the respondent authorities before depriving him of his land, have not initiated any proceedings under Section 146 or 147 of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation Act, 1955 and as such, the action of the respondent authorities is in clear violation of Article 300-A of the Constitution of India.
6. Counter-affidavit on behalf of respondent Nos.3 and 4 filed.

7. By the counter-affidavit filed by respondents Nos.3 and 4, it is stated that the said respondent authority had not acquired any land in Mailardevpally village for four laning of NH-44 (NH-7 old)
from K.M. 9.400 to K.M.22.300 of Hyderabad - Bangalore Section and that whatever land the said authority had acquired, necessary compensation was paid to the land owners as per the awards S. Ramakrishna Reddy vs The Greater Hyderabad Municipal ... on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191287781/
1 passed by the Revenue Divisional Officer, Chevella Division, Ranga Reddy District.
8.

sentences.text: This Court, on 31-01-2024 while noting that the road which has been laid at Mylardevpally village is within the limits of Rajendranagar Circle, GHMC, had directed respondent Nos.1 and 2 to inform this Court as to which of the instrumentalities of the State are responsible for laying the road, failing which it was noted that the same would be understood as having been laid by a third party by encroaching on to petitioner's land and thereby petitioner would be entitled to take steps to remove the said road laid and take possession of property.
On noting as aforesaid, the learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 and 2 sought time to get instructions in the matter.

9. Thereafter, on 21-02-2024 learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 and 2 informed this Court that the authorities have now issued notice dated 01-02-2024 to the petitioner calling upon him to submit documents along with link documents relating to the subject property for the authorities to cause verification, and the aforesaid communication was sent to the petitioner at the last known address by Professional Couriers.
On the aforesaid statement being made to this Court, learned counsel for the petitioner informed that no such communication has been received.
Accordingly, this Court directed the learned Standing Counsel to handover copy of the communication dated 01-02-2024 as issued by the authority to enable the petitioner to comply with the same.

10. Since, respondent Nos.1 and 2, after lapse of 16 long years of the pendency of the present Writ Petition, having informed this Court of the authorities finally taking action by issuing notice to verify as to the correctness or otherwise of the claim of the petitioner of his land being taken by the respondent authorities for the purpose of laying of 150 feet wide road, this Court is of the view that in the event of petitioner furnishing information pursuant to the notice dated 01-02-2024, the respondent authorities are to be directed to initiate action for acquiring the extent of land from which the petitioner was dispossessed by initiating proceedings under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

12. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending if any shall stand closed.
